editorial:
If you have ever felt like the world is moving too fast and you just need to pause, this movie gets you. It follows Craig, a stressed-out teenager who checks himself into an adult psychiatric ward hoping for a quick fix. Instead, he meets a group of patients who change how he sees his own problems. Zach Galifianakis plays a fellow patient who becomes an unlikely mentor, and Emma Roberts adds warmth as a young woman Craig connects with. The tone is surprisingly light for such heavy subject matter, mixing real humor with honest emotion.

The acting is the real highlight here. Galifianakis shows real range beyond his usual comedy roles, and Keir Gilchrist makes Craig feel genuine and relatable. The pacing is gentle and never drags, though some subplots feel a bit rushed. It is not a perfect film, but it handles mental health with care and heart. If you enjoy character-driven stories with a hopeful message, this one is for you. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: Craig spends his week in the ward learning from the other patients and realizes his problems are real but manageable. He leaves with a new outlook, starts taking his medication, and decides to pursue art school instead of the high-pressure path he was on. He also begins a relationship with Noelle. The final scenes show him feeling hopeful and more in control of his life, with a sense that recovery is ongoing but possible.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven stories with a hopeful message.
